thread.title: Apple: After Tax Break, A Netflix Acquisition? - Barron's

title: Apple: After Tax Break, A Netflix Acquisition? - Barron's
text:
Could an expected windfall of billions of dollars from the tax break on repatriated overseas cash rekindle Apple's ( AAPL ) apparent flirtation with an acquisition of Netflix ( NFLX )? GBH Insights , in a report today, thinks so.
Illustration: Bloomberg News Here's its theory: Some $500 billion to $600 billion of cash among Apple, Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Cisco Systems ( CSCO ), Oracle ( ORCL ) and Qualcomm ( QCOM ) is sitting overseas. Ultimately, $300 billion to $400 billion will be repatriated this year, with Apple likely to bring back $200 billion to spend in several ways.
Daniel Ives , head of technology research at GBH, speculates:
The burning question on the Street’s mind is does (Apple CEO Tim) Cook make a big bet with this infusion of cash and do a larger deal (e.g. Netflix) to catalyze and jump start its streaming video/content business. Of course, Apple rarely makes big acquisitions, with the notable exception of Beats Music ( $3 billion in 2014) , opting for acquisitions of start-ups specializing in artificial intelligence, augmented reality and other emerging technologies. That would leave it other ways to spend a cash hoard, probably with accelerated dividends and another dividend hike, according to GBH.
